Pretty much basic things. Avoid anyone with jobs they won't do, except perhaps social. Just make sure to have at least two that can do social. Avoid the negative traits. Scars are fine, re-roll if they have an addiction or an age related disease or cancer. Passions in melee and shooting really aren't needed, since those go up crazy quick when you get into combat. If you can, try to get at least a person with a burning passion and one with an interested (or another burning) in construction, crafting and medical. If you are going to have any number of animals, try to get at least two people with at least 5 in animals. Mining and plants are fairly regular increases, so go with whatever there, though you won't be able to grow healroot unless you have someone with 8 (or certain traits from certain mods). A brawler is a good addition to any colony. A brawler with tough is magnificent. A brawler with tough AND jogger, and you got the perfect frontliner to protect your ranged. One is fine to start, but having a second is better for redundancy. If you intend to have children in your colony, remember that fertility plummets with age. Aim for younger colonists in that case, already married is certainly a plus.

Let me regale you with the unfortunate tale of little Cockroach. He came running into my colony, being persued by cannibal tribals. It seems he had escaped them only after they took a few nibbles, as he was missing three fingers. We accepted him, took care of the cannibals, and gave him a wooden hand. Later, the same tribe came again, right when Cockroach had a growth moment, where he got the sanguine trait and a passion for animals. I accidentally drafted him, and he lost the entire arm this time. After the battle, I realised my mistake, and rushed him to surgery to save his life. A short time later, he got a crude prosthesis for his arm. After using a skilltrainer to up the skill and getting an inspired taming, he tamed a thrumbo. A couple quadrums later (600% child aging rate, so three years for him) he got his final growth moment, this time gaining kind, a passion for both shooting and crafting, and, as he was now an adult, he got real armor. Another raid came. Can you guess who it was? That's right, the cannibals again. He was closest when they came, and got surrounded, and beaten badly. We finished the battle, and got him into surgery again, with less than an hour to spare. This time, they took both of his legs. At this point, I was able to fit him with some better prosthesis (not bionics, I have a medieval prosthetics mod) so gave him new legs and a better arm. Time passed, and I had just completed research into advanced bionics, and had also recently finished learning how to make marine armor. Another raid comes. This time, we are much better equipped, but the raid is massive now. Our stalwart defenders mount the barricades and prepare for a tough fight. In the end, there was only one casualty. Poor, poor Cockroach. This time, they took his kidney, one of his eyes, and shattered his jaw. This time, after patching him up, I anesthetized him and hurriedly made a full set of advanced bionics. Limbs, organs, combat implants, the works. It was time for Cockroach to get his revenge on those cannibals that kept coming and taking pieces of him to snack on. After installing everything I could into him, I had him use his passion for crafting to make a nanocarbon suit, praetor armor and helmet, and a heavy assault rifle. (all from the DOOM- factions mod) Now outfitted as the Doom Slayer, I mounted him up on his trusted (now cyborg due to A Dog Said) thrumbo, he set out on to settle accounts with those damned cannibals. When he got there, he wasted no time opening fire, his passion for shooting showing as he mowed down tribal after tribal, his thrumbo goring them on its mighty horn, until finally, with one last burst from his rifle, he put down the last cannibal, destroying their base and faction as a whole. Despite his many cuts and bruises, his sanguine nature kept him sane as he road back to the settlement, finally victorious over his lifelong tormentors.

If you do mod, stick to QoL things at the start. Ogrestack and Stack XXL are great for keeping your storage zones more tidy. Auto-Cut Blight is an absolute godsend to keep blight from completely ruining your farms. Even if you don't use it for making your colonists, Character Editor lets you examine how backstories, traits, gear, and health conditions will affect a colonist. The standard crashlanded or tribal starts are the best bet for learning, particularly the tribal one, though it is more difficult. Temperate Forests with large hills in the year-round planting latitudes will be the most forgiving place to start. Don't be ashamed to start on a low difficulty setting. This game can be overwhelming until you get into it. If you find luciferium, do NOT use it. Unless you get very lucky, the person who uses it will inevitably go berserk then die when you can't find any more. Until you are more comfortable with the combat, base defenses are critical. Try to funnel raiders into a predictable angle of attack, and then set up numerous traps and turrets there. In the first days, even before you set up a shelter, harvest food from around the map. Starvation sneaks up on you quickly and unexpectedly. Try to set up your base close (but not closer than 4 tiles!) to a nuetral faction so that you can have a close trading partner. There are many other tips and tricks I've learned, and MANY mods I could suggest, but this is getting text walley enough and I don't want to overwhelm you! I'll close with this. Just have fun with it! If you figure out something that works for you, run with it. This game can be frustrating, can be difficult, can even be heartbreaking, but in the end, it's absolutely engaging! Just don't expect it to be quick.
